Reminders in Preparation for Maine eCourts and eFiling in Hancock and Washington County Courts

Date: 7/24/2026

On Monday, July 27, 2026, the Maine Judicial Branch is expanding Maine eCourts to all case types in Judicial Region 7, comprising Hancock and Washington County Unified Criminal Dockets (UCDs), Hancock and Washington County Superior Courts, and Ellsworth, Calais, and Machias District Courts.

All case types -- civil, family, juvenile and criminal cases -- will be included in the transition from paper filing to electronic filing. As of Monday, July 27, all mandatory electronic filers pursuant to the Maine Rules of Electronic Court Systems (MRECS) will be required to eFile documents in these courts. Self-represented litigants (parties who do not have attorneys) who file fewer than six cases in a calendar year will not be required to eFile.

Court Closures and Emergency Filing Procedures
To prepare for the implementation of Maine eCourts and eFiling on July 27, Region 7 courts are operating on a modified schedule and have emergency filing procedures in place. As a reminder, Monday, July 27th through Friday, July 31st is an Administrative Week, and all courts will be closed from 8 a.m. to noon. Please refer to the schedule of closures and emergency procedures during these closings: https://www.courts.maine.gov/ecourts/maine-ecourts-region7-notice-closures.pdf

ShareFile Discontinued in Region 7 Courts
The ShareFile platform used in Region 7 courts are now disabled for all criminal, civil violation, and juvenile filings, as well as GAL vouchers, and attorney billing procedures, as of 2:00 p.m. on Thursday, July 23. Starting Monday, July 27, attorneys must instead use eFileMaine.

Training Resources
For attorneys and staff who are new to using eFileMaine, we highly recommend viewing the recorded videos, particularly the video excerpts, available on the Maine eCourts Trainings and Resources web page. In addition to the recordings, the information and resources available on the Maine eCourts Trainings and Resources web page offer guidance for setting up your eFileMaine account and instructions to eFile documents successfully.

Personal Identifying Information (PII) Attachment (CR-CV-JV-297)
Pursuant to the Maine Rules of Electronic Court Systems (MRECS) filers are responsible for omitting or redacting nonpublic information in electronically filed documents. If the filer decides to omit rather than redact, the personal identifying information must be included on this form. The PII form should be uploaded as an attachment to the associated filing document, in the same way that an exhibit is submitted. Download PII form here

Support
Support for eFiling is available by emailing ecourtshelp@courts.maine.gov or by calling (207) 213-2813, Monday through Thursday from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.

For more information on Maine eCourts and eFiling, visit: https://www.courts.maine.gov/ecourts/index.html

entry.title: US Department of Labor finds child labor and wage violations at 3 San Antonio bakery and café locations
entry.content: SAN ANTONIO – The U.S. Department of Labor has recovered thousands in back wages and assessed penalties after a federal investigation revealed child labor, minimum wage, and overtime violations by the operators of three La Panaderia Bakery & Café locations in San Antonio.The department’s Wage and Hour Division investigated the pay practices of Tequila Almond Croissant LLC, Pan Dulce LLC, and SA Bakery Co. LLC. All three do business as La Panaderia Bakery & Café in San Antonio with locations at 301 E. Houston Street; 17030 Fiesta Texas Drive; and 8305 Broadway.Division investigators found the employers violated child labor provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act. Specifically, they employed a 13-year-old minor who was under the legal age for employment and permitted a 15-year-old minor to work overnight, which is prohibited for 14- and 15-year-olds. The division assessed a $25,706 civil money penalty for the child labor violations.The division’s investigation also revealed minimum wage violations due to the employers’ failure to pay one worker for two overnight shifts at the La Cantera café location on Fiesta Texas Drive. The employers also failed to combine hours for employees who worked at multiple café locations and paid the employees straight-time rates instead of the required time-and-one-half overtime rates. Employers and workers can contact the division with questions and requests for compliance assistance at its toll-free helpline, 866-4US-WAGE (487-9243). Employers are also encouraged to use the agency’s industry-specific compliance assistance toolkits to learn about their responsibilities under the laws enforced by the division. The agency’s PAID program offers employers an opportunity to self-report and resolve potential minimum wage and overtime violations under the FLSA, as well as certain potential violations under the Family and Medical Leave Act.Download the agency’s free timesheet app for iOS and Android devices to track hours and pay.

2026 Maine Hire-A-Vet Campaign Kicks Off August 20!

You're invited! Are you looking for a new career? Maybe you are transitioning from military service, or just looking for a change?

Maine's annual Hire-A-Vet Campaign is a statewide effort with the goal of at least 100 employers hiring at least 100 veterans and military family members during a 100-day period.

The 2026 campaign kicks off Thursday, August 20, at the Augusta National Guard Armory and will be followed by monthly in-person hiring events throughout the state:

  • August 20th, 2026 from 10:30 a.m. to 3 p.m. - Hiring and Veteran Resource Event at the Augusta National Guard Armory, 179 Western Ave, Augusta

  • October 15th, 2026 from 11a.m. to 3 p.m.- Maine Hire-A-Vet - Hiring and Veteran Resource Event at the York County Regional Training Center, 79 First County Way, Alfred

  • November 12th, 2026 from 11a.m. to 3 p.m. - Maine Hire-A-Vet - Hiring and Veteran Resource Event at the Norway Armory, 23 Elm St., Norway

While the campaign is focused on veterans and their families, these events are open to ALL jobseekers!

The Maine Hire-A-Vet campaign provides support and resources to connect veterans with employers through a network of state and federal agencies, resources and nonprofits, education on military language and culture, recruiting and hiring assistance, and recognition for the hiring and advancement of veterans and military family members.

Learn more at https://www.myworksourcemaine.gov/pages/maines-hire-vet-campaign

entry.title: US Department of Labor finds urgent care employer failed to pay over $113K in owed wages to workers for required orientation, meetings, training
entry.content: ATLANTA – The U.S. Department of Labor has recovered $113,199 in back wages after an investigation found a Richmond Hill urgent care facility failed to pay its workers for hours worked and retaliated against a worker for questioning its pay practices.An investigation by the department’s Wage and Hour Division found that Premier Health Consultants LLC – operating as St. Joseph Candler Urgent Care – violated the Fair Labor Standards Act by paying straight time instead of time and one-half in overtime for all hours worked over 40 when employees were required to attend mandatory orientation, meetings, and training. The employer also required certain employees to work off the clock, resulting in unpaid overtime, and suspended a worker who questioned pay practices, all violations of the FLSA.Workers and employers can call the Wage and Hour Division with questions and requests for compliance assistance at its toll-free helpline, 866-4US-WAGE (487-9243). Employers are encouraged to use the agency’s industry-specific compliance assistance toolkits to learn about their responsibilities under the laws enforced by the division. The agency’s PAID program offers employers an opportunity to self-report and resolve potential minimum wage and overtime violations under the FLSA, as well as certain potential violations under the Family and Medical Leave Act. Learn more about the Wage and Hour Division, including a search tool that workers can use if they think they may be owed back wages collected by the division. Download the agency’s free timesheet app for iOS and Android devices to track hours and pay.

Maine eCourts Scheduled to be Implemented in Cumberland County Courts in September

Date: 8/4/2026

The Maine Judicial Branch announced today that the schedule for transitioning courts in Cumberland County (comprising Judicial Region 2) from paper filing to electronic filing (eFiling) is scheduled for Monday, September 28, 2026. The next implementation includes all case types in the Cumberland County Unified Criminal Docket (UCD), Cumberland County Superior Court, Portland District Court, and Bridgton District Court.

You are invited to join a Maine Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) briefing to learn about plans to implement federal changes to Medicaid (in Maine, MaineCare) eligibility that will go into effect on January 1, 2027.   

During this webinar, the DHHS Office for Family Independence (OFI) and Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) will provide an overview of upcoming changes to MaineCare eligibility for Expansion Adults: 

  • New Work Requirements;  

  • Coverage renewals every 6 months instead of every 12 months; and 

  • Retroactive coverage of 1 month instead of 3 months. 

MaineCare Expansion members are adults between 19 and 64 years old who get MaineCare based on their income. They do not meet the Social Security disability guidelines or have Medicare. OFI and OMS will also provide an update on planning for implementation and communications.   

We are also pleased to share the Partner Communications Toolkit, which can be found at MaineCare.gov/work. This toolkit includes materials you can download and print or include in your digital and social media channels to reach the populations in your community that will need to know more and take action to meet the new federal Work Requirements for Medicaid.

  • Late 2026 and through 2027: OFI will provide direct 1:1 phone call outreach to impacted MaineCare Expansion Adults ahead of their renewal month.

Upcoming Federal Changes to MaineCare Eligibility for Some Non-citizens

Aug 20, 2026

We are writing to inform you about an upcoming change to MaineCare eligibility that may affect some of your MaineCare patients. This change is required by federal legislation signed into law in July 2025 (also called H.R.1, One Big Beautiful Bill, P.L.119-21, or Working Families Tax Cuts Act) that made changes to the Medicaid program nationally. These changes apply in all states, including Maine.

Beginning October 1, 2026, MaineCare eligibility is changing for some noncitizen groups. As a result, some individuals who currently receive full MaineCare benefits will no longer qualify for full coverage and will instead be eligible only for Emergency Services MaineCare. An explanation of covered benefits under Emergency Services MaineCare is available in the MaineCare Benefits Manual, Chapter 1, Section 1.02-4(D).

These changes will not affect children under age 21, or pregnant individuals through 12 months after the end of their pregnancy. Please note that the Office for Family Independence (OFI) is still completing the state rulemaking process to implement these federal requirements.

What You Should Know:

  • The eligibility changes are expected to take effect on October 1, 2026.
  • Members who are affected will receive a formal Notice of Decision from OFI before any eligibility changes take place. These notices are expected to be mailed in September 2026.
  • Some members received an early awareness letter in June or July 2026 to let them know they may be affected. This letter was informational only and is not an eligibility determination.

How You Can Help:

As a trusted healthcare provider, you can play an important role in helping your patients prepare for these changes by:

  • Encouraging patients to read any letters they receive from MaineCare or OFI.
  • Reminding patients to report any changes to their immigration status to OFI if it has changed since May 2026, as this could affect their eligibility.
  • Encouraging patients to continue using their MaineCare benefits to access covered healthcare services, including getting checkups and preventive care and refilling prescriptions, while they remain eligible.
  • Helping reassure patients that an early awareness letter does not mean their coverage has already changed.

Resources:

We developed resources to help providers understand these federal changes and answer patient questions. You can find these resources in this linked toolkit.

MaineCare and OFI will continue to share updates through provider e-messages and our webpage and other typical communication channels as additional information becomes available.

See the Non-citizen Resource Guide for resources that you can share with your patients to help support them in preparing for this change, and after their full MaineCare coverage ends. This list will be continually updated as we become aware of new resources.

If you have additional resources for us to add, please email MaineCare at Communications.MaineCare@maine.gov

If members have questions about covered services, please have them call Member Services at 1-800-977-6740.

Thank you for your continued partnership and for helping to ensure MaineCare members receive accurate information and access to the care they need.

entry.title: Expanding Affordable Housing in Maine
entry.content:
Hello, this is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

You know, we want every person at every stage of their life to be confident they can rent or buy a home that's the right size for their family and for their budget and be able to stay there as long as they want. No one should be afraid that a sudden rent increase will break their budget or that someone will buy the land right out from under them and raise rents.

When Hidden Circle Mobile Home Park in Jay went up for sale, that's exactly what the residents were afraid of: someone hiking up the rent and eventually pushing people out of their homes.

According to the 2024 data, nearly 10 percent of Maine people live in manufactured housing, including mobile home communities. Forty-five thousand people in Maine live in a mobile home park. Out-of-state companies have started buying up some of Maine's mobile home parks and then significantly raising rents, in some cases as high as 50 percent. 

And rent increases don't necessarily mean nicer parks either, no improvements necessarily. Corporations know that residents can't easily pick up their home and move it elsewhere, no matter how much the company neglects the park. As one resident in Jay said, "At one time, the park used to look nice. Now they've stopped that, and yet they have increased our rent. If this continues to have higher lot rent payments, then I'm not going to be able to live where I am."

The buying up of mobile home parks by out-of-state entities is a nationwide trend, but here in Maine, we're doing something about it. Last year, we enacted the "Right of First Refusal" law, which requires that residents of a mobile home park be given a chance to purchase their park if they can put together a matching offer when it's put up for sale. That measure strengthened our 2023 "Opportunity to Purchase" law, which required that residents of a mobile home park be allowed to present a competitive offer to buy their park if it's put up for sale.

Well, earlier this week, I visited Jay to celebrate the first residents to take advantage of our new "Right of First Refusal" law to purchase their park, instead of being left to the whims of an out-of-state buyer. Hidden Circle is now the 14th resident-owned manufactured home community in Maine. Resident-owned—isn't that great?

In addition to financing from the Genesis Fund and Maine Community Foundation, Hidden Circle Mobile Home Community was able to make the $1 million purchase to protect these 31 lots with $310,000 as well from our Mobile Home Park Preservation Fund.

My Administration and the Legislature dedicated $8 million in total in recent years to MaineHousing to create this Mobile Home Park Preservation Fund to assist residents in purchasing their own mobile home parks. With that funding, more than 900 homes are expected to be preserved across six parks from Brunswick to Bangor, Turner to Saco.

Last month, nation-leading laws to further protect mobile home park residents took effect in Maine, including laws to limit rent increases, laws to make it easier to expand mobile home parks, and laws creating a way for mobile homeowners to obtain a mortgage—and that could save them hundreds of dollars every month in housing costs.

I was proud to sign those bills into law earlier this year to protect residents in Jay and other towns across Maine from predatory, out-of-state companies. Now, the residents of Hidden Circle Park in Jay have control over how much rent to charge and how that money will be spent. They have control over their common infrastructure, and they can make improvements as they see fit.

Well, we still have a lot more work to do to protect Maine people and mobile home parks from being exploited by companies who simply want to use them to extract a profit, but I am proud of how we worked together with the Legislature to preserve this vital form of housing for people in Maine.

This is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

2027 MaineCare Eligibility Changes: Information, Resources, and Partner Briefing

Aug 21, 2026

The federal government is making changes to MaineCare (Maine’s Medicaid program). These changes apply to Medicaid programs across the country. Last week the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) sent out a Save-the-Date for an August 24, 2026, partner and provider briefing on upcoming changes to MaineCare eligibility. There is still time to register!  

The Office for Family Independence (OFI) and OMS are working together to implement these changes as smoothly as possible to avoid disruptions in coverage for eligible Mainers. Our goal is to provide Mainers with clear, accurate, and actionable information so they can confidently understand how these changes may affect them. 

What is changing?  

As of January 1, 2027, the following MaineCare eligibility changes will start:   

For MaineCare Expansion adults:  

  • New Work Requirements; and  

  • Eligibility renewals every 6 months instead of every 12 months.  

For all MaineCare members:  

  • Reductions in retroactive coverage.   

MaineCare Expansion members are adults between 19 and 64 years old who have MaineCare based on their income. They do not meet the Social Security disability guidelines or have Medicare.

What can MaineCare Members Do Now? 

The most important things MaineCare members can do right now are: 

  • Keep their contact information up to date with OFI,  

  • Read any letters they receive, 

  • Continue renewing their coverage as required, and  

  • Continue using their MaineCare benefits. 

We know that members rely on their healthcare providers for trusted information about MaineCare. We appreciate the value that adds, as well as the additional work. Our goal is to support providers through these changes

PROCESS FOR APPOINTMENT AS A BAIL COMMISSIONER
Bail Commissioners are appointed by the Chief Judge of the District Court and serve at the pleasure of the Court. They must be available to work on an irregular on-call schedule including nights, weekends, and holidays. Appointments are made after review of an application, reference calls, a background investigation, and a determination by the Chief Judge as to the need for a Bail Commissioner in the area where the applicant lives.
Persons who are currently employed by, or have a family member currently employed by, the following agencies/businesses, are not eligible to apply: • A Law enforcement agency; • A Jail/correctional facility; • A Law firm; • The Department of Corrections; • A Prosecutor’s office; • A regional communications/dispatch center; and/or • A Town/City, County, State, or Federal government agency that has a law enforcement agency under its supervision. If appointed as a Bail Commissioner, each applicant must do the following before being allowed to begin their duties: • Attend a mandatory training; • Pass a fingerprint-based FBI criminal history background check; • Complete an online certification to view Criminal Justice Information; • Job shadow an experienced bail commissioner; and • Open a dedicated bail commissioner bank account.

entry.title: 10th Anniversary of the Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument - August 24
entry.content:
WHEREAS, on August 24, 2016, the eve of the National Park Service’s 100th anniversary, President Barack Obama officially designated 87,500 acres of Maine’s North Woods as the Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument; and

WHEREAS, for thousands of years, this land has been home to Wabanaki people who traversed the Penobscot’s waterways and negotiated the deep woods in search of food, furs, medicines and other resources; and

WHEREAS, countless others have come to know the beauty and serenity of this land that native peoples had already known for centuries – those like Henry David Thoreau, Theodore Roosevelt and Percival Baxter – who helped share this special place with the world and commanded us to preserve it; and 

WHEREAS, this land has also been vital to generations of Maine people who make their living by logging and working in the forest products industry; and 

WHEREAS, the establishment of the monument would not have been possible without the lifelong dedication of Roxanne Quimby and her family to preserve this precious piece of Maine, along with the conservationists, philanthropists, and advocates who continue supporting it, including the Friends of Katahdin Woods & Waters; and

WHEREAS, since its creation, the monument has greatly benefited neighboring communities as visitors from in and out of Maine travel to experience its beauty, and in 2024 alone, visitors spent $2.7 million in local communities near the park; and

WHEREAS, with the Katahdin Woods and Waters Monument, we have safeguarded this place that has meant so much to so many people, ensuring that everyone can come camp, hike, fish, take in a night sky, or just enjoy nature in its purest form for generations to come;

NOW THEREFORE, be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim August 24, 2026 as the 

10th Anniversary of the Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument

and I urge everyone to visit the monument, embrace the raw beauty of Maine, and do their part in protecting and preserving our natural environment. 

In testimony whereof, I have caused 
the Great Seal of the State to be 
hereunto affixed GIVEN under my 
hand at Augusta this twentieth day 
of August Two Thousand Twenty-Six

Bradbury Mountain State Park Selected as 2026 Leave No Trace Spotlight; Community Events Set for September 3-5

August 26, 2026

Three days of activities will bring together Leave No Trace, Maine State Parks, volunteers, and community partners to celebrate and care for one of Maine's treasured outdoor spaces.

Pownal - The Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry (DACF) announced today that Bradbury Mountain State Park in Pownal has been selected as a 2026 Leave No Trace Spotlight, bringing three days of community events, outdoor education, and hands-on stewardship to the park and surrounding area September 3-5, 2026.

"Bradbury Mountain is a place people return to again and again, to hike, bike, gather with family, take in the view, and enjoy being outside," said Chris Silsbee, Manager of Bradbury Mountain State Park. Being selected as a Leave No Trace Spotlight gives us a great opportunity to bring the community together, have some fun, and put stewardship into action. Whether you join us for trivia, sit around the campfire, or spend Saturday working on a trail, there's a way for everyone to be part of it.

Activities begin Thursday evening in Freeport and continue through Saturday at Bradbury Mountain State Park.

  • September 3, 2026: Leave No Trace Trivia Night
  • September 4, 2026: Fireside with the Ranger, Leave No Trace Staff & Hot Dog Roast
  • September 4, 2026: Leave No Trace Outreach Tent
  • September 5, 2026: Leave No Trace Event & Stewardship Project
  • September 5, 2026: Leave No Trace Stewardship Project

There is also a special incentive for early arrivals: the first 25 cars through the park gate whose driver says, "Bigfoot Leaves No Trace at Bradbury," will receive a gift bag featuring items from local event sponsors.

About the Leave No Trace Spotlight Program

Each year, Leave No Trace selects nominated outdoor areas for its Spotlight program, which brings communities together to care for and protect places people love to visit. Spotlights combine education, community outreach, and hands-on stewardship to help address impacts from outdoor recreation while giving visitors practical tools they can use long after the event ends. Bradbury Mountain State Park's Spotlight is supported by the Subaru/Leave No Trace Traveling Team, Maine State Parks, community volunteers, and local partners.

About Bradbury Mountain State Park

Bradbury Mountain State Park, located in Pownal, is one of Maine's original five state parks. The park offers more than 20 miles of trails for hiking, mountain biking, and horseback riding, along with camping and opportunities to experience the area's natural and cultural history. The summit of Bradbury Mountain provides expansive views and is a popular location for observing the annual migration of hawks and other birds of prey. For information about Bradbury Mountain State Park, visit the Maine State Parks website.

entry.title: Ovarian Cancer Awareness Month - September
entry.content:
WHEREAS, ovarian cancer is the fifth leading cause of cancer deaths of women in the United States, and it causes more deaths than any other gynecologic cancer; and


WHEREAS, the American Cancer Society estimates that 21,010 cases of ovarian cancer will be newly diagnosed in 2026 and that 12,450 individuals will die from the disease nationwide, including 100 new cases and 70 deaths in Maine; and


WHEREAS, many people are unaware of the symptoms of ovarian cancer, which can often include bloating, pelvic or abdominal pain, difficulty eating or feeling full quickly, urinary issues, and several more that are easily confused with other diseases; and

WHEREAS, the lack of an early detection test for ovarian cancer combined with its vague symptoms means that approximately 80 percent of cases of ovarian cancer are detected at an advanced stage; and

WHEREAS, all women are at risk for ovarian cancer, but approximately 20 percent of women who are diagnosed with ovarian cancer have a hereditary predisposition to the disease which places them at even higher risk; and

WHEREAS, the family history of a woman has been found to play an important role in accurately assessing their risk of developing ovarian cancer, and medical experts believe that family history should be taken into consideration during the annual well-woman visit of any woman; and

WHEREAS, ongoing investments in ovarian cancer research and education and awareness efforts are critical to closing these gaps and improving survivorship for women with ovarian cancer; 

NOW THEREFORE, be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim September 2026 as 

Ovarian Cancer Awareness Month

throughout the State of Maine, and I urge all citizens to recognize this observance.

entry.title: Maine’s Annual Hire-A-Vet Campaign
entry.content:
Hello, this is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

You know, one of the great privileges of serving as your Governor is working with so many veterans to make sure they have all the opportunities that they deserve in our state. Our state is proud that we have one of the highest number of veterans per capita of any state in the country. And we're here to serve them.

I am proud to have the benefit of a number of veterans in my Administration, including members of the Cabinet like Commissioner Randy Liberty, Commissioner Mike Sauschuck, Commissioner and Adjutant General Diane Dunn, as well as a wonderful group of Aide de Camp who advised me and my Administration on issues relating to veterans.

I also come from a proud military family. Two uncles who fought in the Pacific in World War II. My brother who served three tours of duty in Vietnam, and my father who served in the Pacific during World War II at the Battle of Leyte Gulf. So I know that when our friends and family members come home from serving on the front lines, they deserve every opportunity to find rewarding careers in the civil sector that utilize their extensive skills, diverse experiences, and their unique training.

Maine's Hire-A-Vet Campaign is a key part of expanding those opportunities. The campaign had ambitious goals last year: 100 days, 100 employers, and 100 veterans hired. And thanks to everyone’s hard work, we achieved those goals, and we place veterans in good-paying jobs in every county in Maine. The employers hiring the most veterans included the State of Maine itself, Bonney Staffing, Northern Light Health, and Bath Iron Works.

Since its inception in 2015, the Hire-A-Vet Campaign has connected more than 2,000 employers with over 2,200 veterans hired. That's incredible.

And to all the businesses who helped make that happen, I say thank you. You folks hired Maine veterans because you recognized what we all know to be true. Veterans know what it means to work as a team and to leave no one behind. They know how to serve with integrity and commitment to a mission while adapting to dangers known and unknown. They have a great work ethic. That sounds like a pretty good employee to me.

Right now, skilled veterans have another chance to find high-quality jobs through our 2026 Hire-A-Vet Campaign. Once again, the goal of the campaign is to get at least 100 veterans hired by Maine employers within 100 days.

Whether you're a veteran returning to Maine or choosing Maine as your new home, or you're a longtime Maine resident making a career change or reentering the workforce, our Hire-A-Vet Campaign can help you with your job search. Just last month, nearly 50 employers participated in a virtual job fair, which included nearly 40 veterans and their family members. Some candidates attended from as far as Florida and Tennessee because, you know, Maine is where people want to be.

We have hiring fairs coming up in Bangor on September 24th, in Alfred on October 15th, and in Norway on November 12th. All jobseekers are invited.

The Maine Department of Labor also has Veterans’ Representatives located across the state year-round to serve you. I strongly encourage veterans who want to take the next step in their career to connect with a local Veterans’ Representative at one of the statewide CareerCenters. Both veterans and employers can also take advantage of the online CareerCenter at 207-623-7981 or at myworksourcemaine.gov.

My Administration will continue to partner with employers, big and small, through the Hire-A-Vet Campaign to make sure every veteran has the opportunity to live, work, and raise a family right here in Maine.

This is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.
